content: The content provided outlines various indicators and guidelines for monitoring and improving health outcomes related to HIV, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and hepatitis B (HBV). 1. Categories of Differentiated Service Delivery (DSD) Models for Antiretroviral Therapy (ART): DSD models for ART are categorized into four groups: group models managed by healthcare workers, group models managed by clients, individual models based at healthcare facilities, and individual models not based at facilities. Each DSD ART model must be assigned to one of these categories to enable data disaggregation. 2. Uptake of DSD ART Models Among People Living with HIV: Eligibility for DSD ART is defined by national guidelines. The category other includes transgender and gender-diverse individuals who identify outside the binary of male or female. It reflects the rollout and implementation of DSD ART models. 3. Retention in DSD ART Models: Retention in DSD ART models is monitored every 12 months after enrollment. This indicator is limited to facilities with electronic health information systems, as paper-based reporting would be burdensome. It includes all individuals on ART in DSD models, regardless of model changes or reductions in antiretroviral drug dispensing. 4. Viral Suppression Among People in DSD ART Models: It is limited to facilities with electronic health systems and complements viral load suppression monitoring for all ART patients. 5. Syphilis Testing Coverage: Testing is essential for identifying individuals who need treatment, preventing vertical transmission, and assessing adherence to national screening guidelines. 6. Syphilis Test Positivity: It helps identify areas requiring additional support and provides early warnings of changes in HIV and STI transmission. Syphilis positivity data are critical for generating national, regional, and global prevalence estimates. 7. Syphilis Treatment Coverage: Prompt treatment improves health outcomes and reduces sexual and vertical transmission of syphilis. 8. Gonorrhea Testing Coverage: Testing identifies individuals who would benefit from treatment and assesses progress in scaling up screening and adherence to national guidelines. 9. Gonorrhea Test Positivity: It highlights areas requiring additional support and provides data for understanding challenges related to antimicrobial resistance. 10. Gonorrhea Treatment Coverage: Prompt treatment reduces sexual and vertical transmission and prevents complications such as pelvic inflammatory disease, infertility, and blindness. 11. Presence of STI Syndromes: Syndromic management improves health outcomes and reduces STI and HIV transmission. 12. Repeat Diagnosis of STI Syndromes: Repeat diagnoses may indicate inadequate treatment, untreated partners, or unsafe sexual practices. 13. Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Testing Coverage: Testing is critical for identifying individuals who need treatment and preventing mother-to-child transmission of HBV. Each of these indicators is essential for monitoring health outcomes, improving care delivery, and addressing the burden of HIV, STIs, and HBV in various populations.
